title: Forming passive sentences 2: verb + -ing or to-infinitive
subtitle: was seen climbing / loved being given
summary: Form the passive when a verb is followed by an -ing form or a to-infinitive, and recognise the patterns that have no passive at all.

lesson.heading: Verb + object + -ing
lesson.text: Verbs followed by object + **-ing** in the active are made passive with **be + past participle + -ing**. The object of the active verb becomes the subject; the -ing form stays.

examples.text: They saw the monkey climbing over the fence. - The monkey **was seen climbing** over the fence.
The man **was observed hiding** a suspicious package under a seat in the train.

lesson.note: Also: bring, catch, hear, find, keep, notice, observe, send, show.

lesson.heading: being + past participle after an -ing verb
lesson.text: Some verbs that can be followed by an **-ing** form can take the passive **being + past participle**. This is how you make the second verb passive rather than the first.

examples.text: The children enjoyed **being taken** to the zoo.
Tarik rather **resented being given** orders by people who had been there only weeks.

lesson.note: Also: avoid, deny, describe, dislike, face, hate, (not) imagine, like, remember, report, resent.

lesson.heading: Patterns with no passive
lesson.text: When a verb is followed in the active by an object made up of a **noun phrase + -ing clause**, there is usually **no passive** at all.

examples.text: I dread him (or his) finding out.

lesson.note: Also: anticipate, appreciate, dislike, forget, hate, imagine, like, (not) mind, recall, remember.

lesson.heading: Verb + object + to-infinitive
lesson.text: This active pattern is made passive with **be + past participle + to-infinitive**. In some contexts both verbs can be passive.

examples.text: Mr Wang has taught Peter to sing for years. - Peter **has been taught to sing** (by Mr Wang) for years.
Changes to the taxation system **are expected to be proposed**.
examples.note: compare the active We expect the government to propose changes ...

lesson.note: Also: advise, allow, ask, believe, consider, expect, feel, instruct, mean, order, require, tell, understand.

lesson.heading: 'Liking' and 'wanting' verbs have no passive here
lesson.text: Some verbs followed by object + to-infinitive in the active have **no** passive form in this pattern.

examples.text: Susan liked Karl to be there.
examples.wrong: Karl was liked to be there

lesson.note: Also: (can't) bear, hate, love, need, prefer, want, wish.

lesson.heading: Verb + to-infinitive + object
lesson.text: This active pattern is made passive with **verb + to be + past participle**. The first verb stays active; only the infinitive becomes passive.

examples.text: Supermarkets started to sell fresh pasta only in the 1990s. - Fresh pasta **started to be sold** by supermarkets only in the 1990s.
The south coast continues to attract holidaymakers. - Holidaymakers **continue to be attracted** to the south coast.

lesson.note: Group (i): appear, begin, come, continue, seem, tend (and start). Group (ii): agree, aim, arrange, attempt, hope, refuse, want.

lesson.heading: Same meaning or a different one?

left.label: Group (i): the meaning is kept
left.text: appear, begin, come, continue, seem, tend, start
examples: People have come to see organic food as something only the wealthy eat.
Organic food has come to be seen as something only the wealthy eat.
= the same idea, told from the other end

right.label: Group (ii): the meaning changes
right.text: agree, aim, arrange, attempt, hope, refuse, want
examples: I wanted to be helped by Petra.
= two different wishes, held by two different people

lesson.text: Ask yourself which verb you want to make passive. The first verb takes be + past participle; the second takes being + past participle or to be + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Inger ___ for over three hours when she went for her dental appointment.
exercises.explanation: be + past participle + -ing: they kept her waiting, so she was kept waiting.

exercises.prompt: When the police first questioned him, Wayne ___ in the robbery.
exercises.explanation: deny takes an -ing form, and the second verb is passive: being involved.

exercises.prompt: The man ___ a suspicious package under a seat in the train.
exercises.explanation: Active: they observed the man hiding ... The -ing form is unchanged in the passive.

exercises.prompt: When the bike hit her, Ana ___ to the ground.

exercises.explanation: Correct. They caught Mrs Dee shoplifting becomes Mrs Dee was caught shoplifting.

exercises.prompt: When I woke up in hospital, I ___ by the snake but nothing after that.
exercises.explanation: remember takes an -ing form; the snake did the biting, so being bitten.

exercises.prompt: They think that over 20,000 people will go to the pop concert. - The pop concert ___ over 20,000 people.
exercises.explanation: be + past participle + to-infinitive: the concert is expected to attract them.

exercises.prompt: Two teenagers yesterday ___ from school after they were found with over a hundred stolen mobile phones.
exercises.explanation: face takes an -ing form, and the school does the expelling: being expelled.

exercises.statement: Karl was liked to be there.
exercises.explanation: Susan liked Karl to be there. 'Liking' and 'wanting' verbs (like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, wish) have no passive in this pattern.

exercises.prompt: Match each active sentence with its passive version.

pairs.left: Kay's questions began to irritate Marco.
pairs.right: Marco began to be irritated by Kay's questions.

pairs.left: The team captain hopes to select Omar.
pairs.right: Omar hopes to be selected by the team captain.

pairs.left: Critics have come to recognise Galdos as one of Spain's greatest novelists.
pairs.right: Galdos has come to be recognised as one of Spain's greatest novelists.

pairs.left: The south coast continues to attract holidaymakers.
pairs.right: Holidaymakers continue to be attracted to the south coast.

pairs.left: Harris has agreed to interview the Finance Minister.
pairs.right: The Finance Minister has agreed to be interviewed by Harris.

exercises.prompt: They said I had to fill in two copies of the customs declaration. - I ___ two copies of the customs declaration.
exercises.explanation: be + past participle + to-infinitive after require.

exercises.prompt: Does each passive sentence keep the meaning of the active version, or change it?

items.text: Marco began to be irritated by Kay's questions.
Omar hopes to be selected by the team captain.
Kathy arranged to be taken to the station by Alastair.
Galdos has come to be recognised as one of Spain's greatest novelists by critics.
Holidaymakers continue to be attracted to the south coast.
The Finance Minister has agreed to be interviewed by Harris.
